_note: Rules this repository enforces mechanically. Every one comes from something that actually went wrong while building it, and each says which. A rule written in prose is advisory; one here is enforced by a PreToolUse hook whether or not anything was read. New candidates enter with "action": "warn" and let .claude/agent-guard.log decide whether they earn a block. Check them with: node claude-plugin/plugins/agent-guard/scripts/check.js --cases .claude/agent-guard.cases.json

rules.message: CI, pipelines and deployment scripts of a client repository are off limits entirely. A broken pipeline costs the user a working day, and no experiment run against their code is worth that. Not even to fix something visibly wrong.

This repository's own CI. Changing it is a deliberate act rather than a tidy-up along the way: the suite it runs is what every measurement in docs/benchmarks/ is checked by. Say what you are changing and why.

This path is inside a client repository. Read them, index them, benchmark against them — do not write to them. Take a copy under ~/ra-scratch/ instead.

If the user asked for this specific change, back the file up first: .agent/, docs/, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are gitignored there and have no history to recover from.
Writing into a client repository through the shell is the same change with a different tool. Copy it to ~/ra-scratch/ and work there.

A pipe between a check and the `&&` that depends on it reads the *pipe's* exit code, not the check's. This has committed a failing suite three times in this project.

Run the gate to a file and test its own status:

    pytest -q > /tmp/gate.log 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -3 /tmp/gate.log
    if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then git commit ...; fi

A heredoc on this machine mangles backslash escapes: `\\n` inside embedded source arrives as a real newline, and the file it writes has unterminated strings. That has broken a test module and a library function four times here.

Use the Write or Edit tool for any content containing escape sequences, and re-grep the result for the escape you meant to write.
WSL wiped /tmp mid-session during an upgrade and destroyed two SCIP oracles, a PHPStan fact dump and every benchmark result file. Put anything that took minutes to build under ~/ra-scratch/ instead.

These documents carry measured numbers, and every one of them names the run that produced it. Editing a figure by hand breaks that link silently, and a number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number.

Change the measurement, re-run it, then write down what came back.

`pkill -f` and `pgrep -f` match the very shell whose command line contains the pattern. A waiter loop built this way never exited because it was itself a match, and an inline `pkill -f` killed its own shell.

Wait on a PID, or choose a pattern the waiter's own command line cannot contain.
